Petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 claiming Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sreerangam Sreenivasulu S/o Late Sreerangam Ramana in the Motor Vehicle accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That, on 14022022 at about 6.30 p.m., Sreerangam Sreenivasulu was travelling in a two wheeler bearing No.AP04 BD6577 at CTM Cross road on Madanapalli Tirupathi main road, H/o CTM of Madanapalli Mandal, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh.

At that time, the driver of tractor bearing registration No.AP39LB3144 and trally No.AP39LL2054 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Sreerangam Sreenivasulu and caused the accident.

Due to the impact,
Sreerangam Sreenivasulu sustained severe injuries all over the body.
Immediately the Sreerangam Sreenivasulu was shifted to Government hospital for treatment and while undergoing treatment he died at 700 p.m. on the same day in the hospital.
Sreerangam Sreenivasulu was aged 31 years as on the date of accident and was working as mason and earning sum of Rs.25,000/p.m.
The respondent No.1 is insurer and respondent No.2 is owner of offending vehicle.
As such, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
3. Notice of this petition was duly served upon both the respondents.
However, the respondent No.1 appeared through its learned advocate and filed written statement.

4. In the objections, the respondent No.1 denies the entire averments made in the petition, age,
avocation of the deceased.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tractortrailer bearing Reg. No.AP39LB3144 and trally No.AP 39LL2054 and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it has contended that accident occurred due to the negligence of deceased himself.
It is also contended that, the compensation claimed is exhorbitant.
With all these contentions it is prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings of the parties, materials placed on record this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri.Sreerangam Sreenivasulu S/o Sreerangam Ramana was died in the Road Traffic Accident which occurred on 14022022 at about 6.30 p.m. at CTM cross road on Madanapalli - Thirupathi main road, H/o CTM of Madanapalli Mandal, Chittoor,Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tractor bearing No.AP39LB 3144 and Trally No.AP39LL2054 by its driver?
2. Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sreerangam Sreenivasulu?

3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4.
What Order or Award?
6. In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents Ex.P1 to Ex.P17 and closed their side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence.
7. Heard arguments of both sides.
Perused the pleadings, evidence and the materials placed on record.

My findings on the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No. 4 : As per the Final Order  for the following :

sentences.text: 9. On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tractor.

10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as P.W.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and reiterated the petition averments.
11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.

Ex.P12 and 13 are the True copies of FIR and complaint which shows that the Madanapalli Police have registered the case against the driver of Tractor bearing No.AP39LB3144 and trally No.AP39LL2054 for the offence punishable under Sections 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.1 is the true copy of IMV Report which shows that accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said motor vehicle.
Ex. P.2 is the true copy of spot sketch which shows that same was drawn by the IO during the course of investigation.

Ex.P.3 is the true copy of the Chargesheet which shows that the I.O of Madanapalli Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Sections 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.4 is true copy of death certificate of Sreerangam Sreenivasulu which justify the fact of his death.
Ex.P.5 is the notarised copy of family members certificate issued by the authority concerned which shows that the deceased has left behind the petitioners herein as his legal representatives.
The documents Ex. P.6 to 11 supports the case of petitioners that they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
The document Ex. P.15 i.e., true copy of PM certificate discloses the fact of death of Sreerangam Srinivasulu and also depicts the cause of death as haemorragic shock.
The contents of Ex. P.17 also supports the fact of death of Sreerangam Srinivasulu and cause of death.
12. PW1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.1.
But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the version of the Petitioners.
13. In order to rebut the evidence of petitioners, respondent No.1 has not adduced any rebuttal evidence.
14. Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioners and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioners have proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tractor bearing No.AP39LB3144 and trally No.AP39LL 2054 and in the said accident and the Sreerangam Sreenivasulu had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Affirmative". Issue No. 2 and 3:
15.

sentences.text: It is stated in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are sons and petitioner No.4 is mother of the deceased Sreerangam Sreenivasulu.
In order to prove this fact, PW.1 has produced Ex.P6 to 11 i.e., Aadhar Card of petitioners and the Aadhar card of the deceased Sreerangam Sreenivasulu and notarised copy of ration card.

The document Ex. P.6 to 10 justifies the fact that the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and the petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased and the petitioner No.4 is mother of the deceased.
Apart from that, the police records also mention regarding the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Upon going through the said documents it clearly shows that the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are the legal heirs of the deceased Sreerangam Sreenivasulu.
Therefore, the Petitioners are considered as the dependents of the deceased Sreerangam Sreenivasulu.
17. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 31 years and his avocation is shown as mason and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
In this regard, petitioners have not produced any supportive documents to show that avocation and income of the deceased.

Therefore,
in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2022, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 15,500/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. Further, the Petitioners have stated the age of the deceased Sreerangam Sreenivasulu as 31 years at the time of the accident.
As per the document Ex.P.10, i.e., notarized copy of Aadhar card of the deceased Sreerangam Sreenivasulu his year of birth is shown as 1991.
The date of accident is 1402 2022.
Hence, the age of the deceased Sreerangam Sreenivasulu is considered as 31 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
20.
The deceased has left behind him, his his wife, sons and mother I.e, petitioner No.1 to 4.

Hence,
the Petitioners No.1 to 4 are considered as the dependents of the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 is wife of the deceased, petitioner No.2 and 3 are sons and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased Sreerangam Sreenivasulu, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rupees 44,000/ each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/ collectively towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/ collectively towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
21.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and she lost her husband's love and care.
Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased and they lost their father's love and care and petitioner No.4 is mother of the deceased and she lost her son's love and care.

Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/
collectively under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
22. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/ collectively under this head would be just and reasonable.

V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
23.

It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was notionally fixed at Rs.15,500/ p.m.
24.

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 31 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.15,500/ comes to Rs.6,200/.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.21,700/ p.m. (Rs.15,500/ + Rs.6,200/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 16.

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 4 to 6, 1/4th of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

25. After deducting 1/4th towards his personal expenses in Rs.21,700/ it comes to Rs.16,275/
(Rs.21,700/  5,425/) and multiplier applied is 16 which comes to Rs.31,24,800/ (16,275 x 12 x 16).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.31,24,800/ towards loss of dependency.

26. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,76,000/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 10,000/ of dead body 6.
Loss of Dependency Rs. 31,24,800/ Total Rs.33,93,800/
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.33,93,800/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

sentences.text: Regarding Liability :
As already discussed in the Issue No.1, in this case the driver of the offending Tractor bearing Reg.No.AP39LB3144 and trally No.AP39LL2054 was charge sheeted.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
Moreover, there is no proof of allegation of the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Therefore, Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 being the owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the "Affirmative" and Issue No. 3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
28. Issue No.4 : From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.33,93,800/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.33,93,800/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 50% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 15% each to the Petitioner No.2 and 3 and 20% to petitioner No.4.
 After the deposit of the Award  amount and interest being made by the  Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 4, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 4 by way of E payment and after their proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 4 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years.
The entire amount awarded to the petitioner No.2 and 3 shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.2 and 3 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank until they attain the age of majority.
